column1: # install-set.tsv: the box manifest. Every file this repository puts on the box,
# where it lands, when it runs, and which deploy or manual step a change needs.
# One table, read by scripts/lib.sh's manifest queries: scripts/deploy.sh routes
# a changed script to its deploy, deploy-mail.sh and deploy-control.sh install
# and remove it, cron-apply.sh schedules it, and check-hygiene.sh compares the
# installed copy with the checkout. Adding, renaming or retiring an installed
#   script         the file in scripts/, a path from the repository root when it
#                  starts with openbsd/, or a compiled binary's name
#                  binary, drain for the directory the drain's own config names,
#                  checkout for a script cron runs from the checkout itself, or
#                  a document root under /home/www for a file httpd serves
#   schedule       the five cron fields, or - when nothing schedules it
#   args           the arguments the cron line passes, empty when there are none
#   deploy_route   comma-separated: the deploys a change needs (mail, control,
#                  relayd, nsd) and the manual steps (cron, env, pf, doas), or
#                  none. A retired row's route is the deploy that removes it.
#   installed_name the name at the destination, - when it keeps its own
#   status         active, or retired for an uninstall step
# A script installed in two places has one line per place. A retired row is a
# destination that must not carry the file: the deploy removes it if present.
# Monday, not Sunday. The run creates a box, restores the snapshot into it and
# mails the operator when it fails, and a failure mailed at 03:45 on a Sunday is
# one nobody can act on until Monday anyway: the day is chosen for the morning
# the mail is read, not for the test.
# Read from the checkout rather than installed, so a pull that fixes one is the
# whole change. Both are weekly and an hour apart, so a failure is one mail.
# Rendered into the capsule by the control deploy, and the finger page written
# by the mail deploy, both from the checkout rather than installed.
# The restore template's installer answers, served from the landing site's
# document root at https://kyriakon.net/install.conf and fetched at the VNC
# console. The source is tracked outside scripts/, so the row names its repo
# path; deploy-mail.sh installs it and check-hygiene.sh compares the served copy
# Operator-run: the plan prints the env step, whether the reason is the script or
# A deploy script's own path needs the deploy it runs.
# The pf fragments live in the script; a change is still the propose-only step.
# Nothing installs or runs these: a change reaches the next run through the pull.
# The drain binary is compiled, installed by deploy-control.sh into sbin and
# scheduled every minute: its line is a row like the scripts', not an arm.
# The crontab it writes is a manual step in addition to its install.
# A helper of the relay deploy and of the drain's web pass.
# The From-header filter is a compiled binary row. deploy-control.sh builds and
# installs it under the name smtpd's proc-exec line uses; the route is control
# for the install, while deploy.sh also plans the mail restart for a source
# change because the running filter keeps the old code until smtpd restarts.
# The key check helper core runs as a process, so the control plane does not
# build pgp. Built from keygen/ and installed under the name core invokes.
# deploy-control.sh installs lib.sh and its modules beside the login checker,
# which sources them; their route is what keeps deploy-mail.sh from taking them.
# The checker runs as root under a doas rule, so it is installed under a name
# without the .sh suffix; the name is the row's, not a private rename table's.
# The ksh From-header filter that #947 replaced. A box that ran it must lose the
# file rather than keep it beside the compiled binary of the same name.
# The pre-split copies in /root/bin that a box from before the control-plane
# split still carries. Each is an uninstall step for deploy-mail.sh.
